description:
FILED s470bt (Opus, 2026-09-06) by the B6 IR conformance corpus.  Ten of the
corpus's 347 cases differ from perl ONLY in this string.

PROBE (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL main cd34df72):

  eval { my $x = 1/0 };        print "A:[$@]";
  my @a; eval { $a[-4] = 1 };  print "B:[$@]";
  eval { die "boom\n" };       print "C:[$@]";
  eval { die "nonl" };         print "D:[$@]";

  perl  A:[Illegal division by zero at /tmp/p.pl line 1.]
        B:[Modification of non-creatable array value attempted, subscript -4 at /tmp/p.pl line 2.]
        C:[boom]  D:[nonl at /tmp/p.pl line 4.]
  PCL   A:[Illegal division by zero at (eval 0) line 0.]
        B:[... subscript -4 at (eval 0) line 0.]
        C:[boom]  D:[nonl at /tmp/p.pl line 4.]

So an EXPLICIT `die "msg"` already gets the right location; a die raised BY THE
RUNTIME (division by zero, non-creatable array value, `Can't "last" outside a
loop block`, `Illegal modulus zero`, `Undefined subroutine &main::X called`)
gets the placeholder `%p-caught-perl-value` supplies.

docs/ir-spec.md 5.4 already NAMES the placeholder ("the placeholder every
runtime die gets"), so this is documented, not unknown -- but it is not
"error text fidelity", which the USER ruled is not a goal: it is the FILE and
LINE, which real programs print, match on and report.  A program that says
`$@ =~ /at \Q$0\E line/` is wrong under PCL today.

SHAPE OF A FIX (not designed): the emitted call site is where the location is
known.  The p-sub frame already carries a caller stack (docs/caller-implementation.md);
what is missing is a per-STATEMENT line, which the compiler has at lowering
time and does not put in the IR.  A cheap first step would be a dynamic
"current statement" (file,line) bound where a statement lowers, which the
runtime's die formatter reads -- measure the cost first, it is on every
statement.

CORPUS CASES (ir-conform/known-fail.tsv): 033-array 034-array 139-local
172-loops-exits 173-loops-exits 201-misc 246-regex 282-sort, plus the
location half of 295-sprintf and 329-string-eval.

=== DONE (s473c) — SIZED + IMPLEMENTED, GATE DEFAULT OFF (Opus, 2026-09-08) ===

THE MECHANISM IS IN THE TREE AND PROBES IDENTICAL TO PERL; it is the Kind-A
gate `line-track` (Pl/Passes.pm) and it is DEFAULT OFF, because the sizing the
s473 brief demanded says it is above the bar the brief set for shipping it on.
THE FLIP IS ONE LINE -- move `line-track` out of %DEFAULT_OFF and into
%NOT_OFF_BY_NONE in Pl/Passes.pm, re-run the gate + sweep + tools/ir-conform,
and take the seven `1240` rows out of ir-conform/known-fail.tsv.

--- WHAT IT IS (perl's PL_curcop, one mechanism) --------------------------
  *p-src-line*     fixnum, written by (p-line N) at the head of EVERY lowered
                   statement.  ONE emission site: Parser2::_lower_block, which
                   handles exactly one statement per recursion, so one form
                   per level IS one per statement on every path.
  *p-src-file-id*  fixnum INDEX into *p-src-files*, written by (p-file "â¦") at
                   a file's run bucket and at every sub BODY; a NEGATIVE id is
                   perl's `(eval N)`.
  p-loc-save       saves and restores the pair on a NORMAL return only (a die
                   must leave them at the die site).  Four location scopes use
                   it: p-sub-frame (so `my $z = f() / 0` reports the CALLER's
                   line), p-eval-block, p-try, p-eval (string eval) and
                   p-load-module-cached (so a require does not leave the
                   module's file behind).
  %p-loc-string    returns NIL when no location was ever recorded, so with the
                   gate off every caller keeps its pre-#1240 answer BYTE for
                   byte (`(eval 0) line 0.` from %p-caught-perl-value, and no
                   location at all from p-die's no-:loc branch).

--- THE MEASUREMENT (the deliverable) ------------------------------------
Instrument: ONE tree, two PCL_OPT settings, the two emissions timed
INTERLEAVED best-of-K against ONE core (tools/bench-emission-ab.pl's method;
the driver is scratch/s473c/optab.pl in the s473c worktree).  Rows are
tools/bench-exec.pl's own, at 20x N for the micro rows so exec is ~0.5 s
against the ~1 s constant term.  Every number below was reproduced twice.

  MACRO rows (real programs -- the brief's <=1 % bar):
      json-rt  -0.52 %      moo-objs +0.23 %      textproc -1.16 %   PASS
  CALL rows:
      subret   +1.53 %      methret  +0.46 %      gcdret   -0.33 %
  MICRO rows (the brief's <=3 % bar), two runs each:
      intloop+=  +0.01 / -0.10      arith   +1.55 / +1.26
      intloop=   +5.84 / +5.11      useint  -2.48 / -2.29
      cfor       +4.09 / +4.33      arrhash +0.00 / +0.19
      collatz    +5.27                                          FAIL (3 rows)

LINEARITY, so the 5 % is not an alignment artefact: 0 / 1 / 2 / 4 stores per
iteration of a 3.7 ns loop body read +0 / +6.71 / +12.81 / +19.66 %.  The cost
is REAL and is ~0.25 ns = about one cycle per statement.  That is 5 % of a
`$s = $s + $_` and under 0.5 % of anything with a hash, a call or a string in
it -- which is why the macro rows cannot see it.

TWO SHAPE FACTS, both measured, both now written into the runtime's header:
  * a SPECIAL costs +13.58 % on intloop where an sb-ext:defglobal costs ~+5 %
    (6 instructions -- TLS index load, bound check, store -- against 2).  So
    the registers are defglobals and nothing may let-bind them.
  * writing the FILE as a STRING to a global pays SBCL's gencgc CARD MARK (6
    instructions against 2, and a second cache line).  Hence the fixnum id,
    interned once per emitted (p-file â¦) through load-time-value.

--- WHY NOT (B), THE COLD-BRANCH CONSTANT ---------------------------------
Every message the corpus names is raised INSIDE a runtime function, not at
the emission boundary: p-/ (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp:4157), p-% (4224, 4236), the
non-creatable-array-value store (4665), the loop-control raiser (12383), the
undefined-subroutine path (1060, 21203, 21490).  Giving any of them the line
means a per-CALL argument on the hot path -- the brief's own STOP condition.

--- WHAT IT BUYS (measured with the gate ON) ------------------------------
tools/ir-conform: SEVEN of the eight #1240 rows PASS -- 033-array, 034-array,
172-loops-exits, 173-loops-exits, 201-exception, 246-exception,
282-loops-exits.  139-local does NOT: its known-fail note says the caught text
also "names the wrong error", which is a second cause and not this register.
With the gate OFF the corpus is unchanged (308 pass / 0 fail / 37 known / 0
stale), and corpus-diff over 111 files is IDENTICAL to main.
Probes (perl 5.40.3, byte-identical): division by zero, negative-subscript
store, `die "boom\n"`, `die "nonl"`, `Can't "last" outside a loop block` from
a called sub, undefined subroutine, `5 % 0`, a die AFTER a call returned
(the frame restore), a die inside a required MODULE, and a runtime die inside
a string eval (`(eval N) line M`).
Guard: Pl/t/die-location-01.t, 6 rows, 7.7 s wall -- every row runs with
PCL_OPT=line-track and the last one asserts the default emission has no
register writes at all.

--- THE FLIP (one line, when the cost is acceptable) ----------------------
Move `line-track` out of %DEFAULT_OFF into %NOT_OFF_BY_NONE in Pl/Passes.pm
(a correctness mechanism belongs in the general form, so `PCL_OPT=none` must
NOT switch it off), re-run gate + full sweep + tools/ir-conform, and drop the
seven annotated `1240` rows from ir-conform/known-fail.tsv (033-array,
034-array, 172/173/282-loops-exits, 201-exception, 246-exception).  139-local
stays: it has a second cause.

--- BARS ON THE FINAL (REBASED) TREE, re-run 2026-09-08 -------------------
gate `PCLXS_DIR=~/pclxs tools/prove-core`: 224 files / 7720 tests, ONLY
  xs-01(5) xs-02(4) xs-03(4) = the standing 13 pclxs rows; 0 WRITE-DATE rows.
full sweep `--jobs 4`: GATE clean, 0 new / 0 fixed, TOTAL passing 18673 (+0),
  drops census 5 / current 5 (+0).
corpus-diff.pl c709804a: emission IDENTICAL over 111 files, silent drops 5
  unchanged, shapes 6/6 identical.
emission-ab --ref c709804a --shapes --list lib/**/*.pm: 27 SAME / 0 DIFF /
  RCDIFF 0.
tools/ir-conform --jobs 2: 308 pass / 0 fail / 37 known / 0 stale (of 345).
ir-host-leak: 31 leaked symbols over 111 files -- the same set as main (the
  emission is byte-identical), no new leak.  tag-license --check clean.
Guard inverse-verified on a `git archive c2016433` extraction: 12/12 fail.
  Stronger inverse probed too -- the base tree and the new tree's DEFAULT both
  answer `at (eval 0) line 0.` for all five corpus dies; the new tree with
  PCL_OPT=line-track answers byte-identically to perl 5.40.3.

--- RESIDUE FILED --------------------------------------------------------
#1359  the module cache key does not include PCL_OPT (found by this work).
#1360  an EXPLICIT die inside a string eval reports `- line 1` (pre-existing),
       and a sub DEFINED inside a string eval reports the caller's file.
#1361  Carp croak/confess/carp/cluck append a bare newline, so every module
       diagnostic loses perl's ` at CALLER line N.` (pre-existing; the
       caller's location is the one thing this register cannot supply).
subject: SILENT WRONG (pre-existing, found by the ir-conform corpus): every RUNTIME-RAISED die carries the placeholder location `at (eval 0) line 0.` where perl names the file and line -- 10 corpus cases print the wrong string
